first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has prior evidence of improving activation and early adoption, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing could counter the competitor but carries documented 30-day retention harm, so it should not be the default response. Verify the two most directly relevant onboarding records before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the onboarding flow. The confirmed evidence directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline: exp_86 improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. Signup simplification also lifted SMB activation and qualified revenue, but its 1% retention decline and SMB-only validation warrant retention guardrails and segment-level analysis. This is more aligned with sustainable long-term qualified revenue than promotional pricing.

final2.rationale: Shift this cycle’s experiment to a tightly targeted pricing response for price-sensitive SMB accounts because the immediate competitive threat and churn signals have materially intensified. Prior evidence shows acquisition and revenue lift in this exact segment, but also materially lower 30-day retention, so limit exposure and require qualified-revenue, retention, and churn guardrails. Do not broadly roll out or treat entry-price matching as a general growth strategy; revisit onboarding next cycle.
